messages.subject_clean: Installing a package from local repository
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am running into difficulties installing a package (that isn't on CRAN) into my local repository. As suggested by http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/limitations.html, I created a ~/R/packages folder and then I installed the vimcom R package into the local repository like this:

download.file("http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/old/vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz", destfile = "vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz")
install.packages("vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz", type = "source", lib = '~/R/packages')

I was successful in doing this. Then in my project, I started R and loaded up packrat (0.4.2-1) and then proceeded to install this package.

library('packrat')
packrat::set_opts(local.repos = "~/R/packages")
packrat::install_local("vimcom")

This returned the following errors:

Installing package from '~/R/packages/vimcom'
Installing vimcom
'/home/fong/usr/local/lib64/R/bin/R' --vanilla CMD INSTALL '/home/fong/R/packages/vimcom'  \
  --library='/share/lustre/fong/projects/relapse_chl/packrat/lib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/3.1.0' --install-tests

Error in pkg$package : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

I remember being able to do this in an earlier release of packrat, yet it is not failing. Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks,

Hi TinyHeero,

I apologize! I mislead you in my earlier recommendations. The way local repositories work in Packrat is that it’s just a folder of (untarred) package sources. What you really want to be doing is placing the package sources, not an installed package tarball, into your ~/R/packages folder.

(If you are already using that folder as a library, ie, directory full of installed packages, you might want to use e.g. ~/R/package-sources or something similar.

Here’s a script that can fix things up:
packrat::opts$local.repos("~/r/package-sources")
dir.create("~/r/package-sources")
download.file("http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/old/vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz", destfile = "vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz")
localRepoDir <- normalizePath("~/r/package-sources")
untar("vimcom_1.0-0.tar.gz", exdir = localRepoDir)
packrat::install_local("vimcom")

packrat::snapshot()

The main difference is that we simply untar, rather than install, the package into the ‘local repository’ directory.

Thanks, and sorry about the earlier misinformation!
Kevin

The issue here is that we use the .Rprofile to pop us into 'packrat mode', which then sets the library paths so that the R session knows where to find the installed packages.

There are a couple workarounds I would try:

    1. Explicitly call `source("<pathToProjectRprofile>")` at the start of the knit session,
    2. Call `packrat::on("<pathToProjectFolder>")` at the start of the knit session.

You could, for example, place these at the top of the .Rmd to ensure that 'packrat mode' is enabled.

Let me know if that helps!

Thanks,
Kevin

    2. 'Releasing' the package so it can be used in non-Packrat R sessions.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yasmin,

When initializing a new project, packrat infers the repositories based on the current value of getOption('repos'), and then caches those (in the lockfile) to be used later.

It seems like you would be able to do such a thing with e.g. options(repos = <localRepos); packrat::init().

For example, if I run:
R --vanilla --slave -e "options(repos = '~/local/cran'); packrat::init()"

I see in the generated lockfile:
Repos: CRAN=~/local/cran

It sounds like this (or some version of this) should suffice for what you need.

Best,
Kevin
